t: Zoroastrianism grew from the hymns of the prophet Zarathustra, who taught that the Wise Lord, Ahura Mazda, calls every person to choose truth over the lie in a cosmic struggle that will end in the triumph of good.

It was the faith of the Achaemenid kings and the state religion of the Parthian and Sasanian empires, and its ideas of judgement, heaven and hell and a final renewal of the world may have influenced Judaism, Christianity and Islam.

After the Arab conquest of Iran it became a minority faith; today it survives among small communities in Iran and among the Parsis of India, whose contribution to modern Bombay was out of all proportion to their numbers.
dyk: The Magi who bring gifts to the infant Jesus in the Gospel of Matthew bear the title of the priests of Iran, the magi, who were the guardians of the Zoroastrian tradition.
ev: Zarathustra composes the Gathas, by the reckoning of many modern scholars; others place him in the 7th or 6th century BCE
Darius I credits his victories to Ahura Mazda in the Behistun inscription
Ardashir I founds the Sasanian Empire, under which Zoroastrianism becomes the state religion
The high priest Kartir organises the Zoroastrian church and its fire temples across the empire
The last Sasanian king, Yazdegerd III, is killed after the Arab conquest of Iran
Zoroastrian priests compile the Pahlavi books, among them the Denkard and the Bundahishn
Zoroastrians from Iran settle in Gujarat, according to the Story of Sanjan: the origin of the Parsis
The Parsi Dadabhai Naoroji becomes the first Asian elected to the British House of Commons

f.origin: Eastern Iran or Central Asia, in the second or early first millennium BCE (the date is disputed)
f.scriptures: The Avesta, whose oldest part is the Gathas, the hymns of Zarathustra; later Pahlavi texts such as the Denkard and the Bundahishn
f.followers: Perhaps 100,000 to 200,000, mainly in India (the Parsis), Iran and the diaspora
